subject: general
question:
**Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.**

It doesn't matter __whether they get__ the job or not.
solution:
The correct answer is: **No improvement required**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence has no errors in it.
 
• **Whether** is a conjunction that is used in reference to a choice or alternatives.
 
• We use **whether** in indirect '**yes-no'** questions and questions with '**or'**.
 
 
• **Example -** *We're not sure **whether **to stay here for dinner or go somewhere else.*
 
 
 
• The given sentence states that **"They get a job or not, it does not make any changes"** For this kind of sentence **'whether' is appropriate to use**.
 
• So, the given sentence is both **grammatically and contextually correct**.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

 

**The complete sentence is:** *It doesn't matter whether they get the job or not.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Use **"nor"** before the second or further of two alternatives when **"neither" introduces the first**.
 
• We use **"if"** to introduce a possible or unreal situation or condition.
 
• We use **"so"** as subordinating conjunction to introduce clauses of result or decision.
